info.title: Adikara API
info.description:
REST JSON API. Log in at `/auth/login` (or `/auth/student/login`), then press **Authorize** and paste the `access_token`.

Endpoints are grouped by role: **Admin**, **Teacher** (admins can use these too), **Student**, and **Shared** (more than one role).

**Seeded accounts** (run `pnpm seed`; every password is `ChangeMe-123`):

| Role | Login | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| ADMIN | `admin@adikara.com` | /auth/login |
| TEACHER | `guru@example.com` | /auth/login |
| USER | `siswa.satu`, `siswa.dua` | /auth/student/login |

**Try the admin role:** log in as `admin@adikara.com`, then `POST /admin/teachers`, `POST /admin/classes` (with that teacher's `id` as `teacher_id`) and `POST /admin/students` (with the class `id` as `class_id`). `GET /admin/classes` lists the seeded class and its id. Details: docs/admin.md.

**Try a live session:** log in as the teacher, `POST /sessions` with `{"class_code": "KELAS7A"}` and note the PIN; log in as `siswa.satu` (second browser profile) and `POST /sessions/join` with the PIN. Details: docs/sessions.md.

Errors always look like `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }`.

tags.name: Admin · teachers
tags.description: Endpoints for admins only. Log in at `POST /auth/login` with an admin account. Create, read, update and delete teacher accounts. Assigning classes to a teacher is done under admin/classes.

tags.name: Admin · students
tags.description: Endpoints for admins only. Log in at `POST /auth/login` with an admin account. Create, read, update and delete student accounts, and put each student in a class. Only the admin can change a student's class, so students cannot end up in a wrong class.

tags.name: Admin · classes
tags.description: Endpoints for admins only. Log in at `POST /auth/login` with an admin account. Create classes and decide which teacher teaches each one. Students are put into classes under admin/students.

tags.name: Teacher · auth
tags.description: Endpoints for teachers (admins can use them too). Log in at `POST /auth/login`. Login for teachers and admins (both log in with email).

tags.name: Teacher · classes
tags.description: Endpoints for teachers (admins can use them too). Log in at `POST /auth/login`. The classes a teacher teaches and their students (read-only; the admin assigns classes and students).

tags.name: Teacher · sessions
tags.description: Endpoints for teachers (admins can use them too). Log in at `POST /auth/login`. Run a live class session with a PIN (like Kahoot) and read attendance. Flow: `POST /sessions` → students `POST /sessions/join` → everyone opens `GET /sessions/{id}/events` → start / lock / end.

tags.name: Teacher · chats
tags.description: Endpoints for teachers (admins can use them too). Log in at `POST /auth/login`. A teacher's chats with the AI. Send text, and optionally a PDF/DOCX/PPTX: the file is stored, read by the worker, and used by this chat only. The AI's reply is written by the worker, so poll `GET /chats/{id}/messages` until `reply_pending` is false.

tags.name: Student · auth
tags.description: Endpoints for students. Log in at `POST /auth/student/login`. Login for students (username and password).

tags.name: Student · sessions
tags.description: Endpoints for students. Log in at `POST /auth/student/login`. Join the live session your teacher started, with its PIN.

tags.name: Shared · auth
tags.description: Endpoints that more than one role uses. The logged-in account, for any role.

tags.name: Shared · sessions
tags.description: Endpoints that more than one role uses. The live event stream of a session, for the teacher who runs it and the students who joined.

post.summary: Send a message (and optionally a file)
post.description:
Send `text` as JSON, or as multipart form data together with a `file`. A file is stored and read by the worker, then used as knowledge of this chat only. Answers 202 at once: the reply arrives later, see `GET /chats/{id}/messages`. If the file cannot be read, the material shows `FAILED` with the reason and the AI says so in its reply.

**For:** Teacher · **Access:** staff (teachers and admins)

**Middleware:** upload:file

post.summary: Join a session with the PIN
post.description:
Marks the student present and notifies the teacher. Calling it again (refresh, second tab) does not create a second entry. After joining, open `GET /sessions/{id}/events` to follow the session live.

Errors: `session_not_found` (wrong, ended or expired PIN), `not_in_class`, `kicked`, `session_locked`.

**For:** Student · **Access:** student (students only (role USER))

**Middleware:** rate-limit:join

get.description:
Reads the account from the database, so the role is always current.

**For:** Shared · **Access:** authenticated (any logged-in account)

A long-lived `text/event-stream`. The first event is always `snapshot` with the current state, so a refresh loses nothing.

| Event | Sent to | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot` | the new connection | current state (teachers also get the participant list) |
| `participant_joined` | teachers | a student joined or came back |
| `participant_left` | teachers | a student dropped (`disconnected`) or was removed (`kicked`) |
| `session_started` | everyone | the teacher pressed Start |
| `session_locked` / `session_unlocked` | everyone | joining was locked or reopened |
| `session_ended` | everyone | the session ended; the stream closes |
| `kicked` | that student | removed by the teacher; the stream closes |

Teachers can follow only their own sessions (admins any). Students can follow only a session they joined. Browsers' `EventSource` cannot send the `Authorization` header, so read the stream with `fetch` (or `@microsoft/fetch-event-source`). Swagger UI cannot display a stream; try it with `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" …/sessions/{id}/events`.

**For:** Shared · **Access:** authenticated (any logged-in account)
